principle: One user-facing API; multiple mathematically distinct kernels; one transactional lifecycle; one capability registry; one complete work/error authority.
non_goal: Do not merge DOPRI5, RODAS5P, Peer-W, BDF, Radau, exponential and geometry-specific methods into one tableau or pretend they share history/controller/stability.

frontend.selection: Explicit method selection first. Auto-selection opt-in only among implemented and qualified methods whose capability predicates and permission constraints match.

transaction.attempt: Clone/stage all method-specific hidden history, controller, solver caches and event state; candidate result is not committed.
transaction.accept: Atomically commit time, state, method history, controller, dense output, events and work exactly once.
transaction.reject: Discard candidate state but retain incurred work and rejection count.
transaction.invalidate: Model/parameter/source epoch changes invalidate method caches unless a verified reset/transfer is invoked.
transaction.stale_attempt: Generation mismatch must reject stale attempt.

derivative_permissions.precedence: User derivative and linear-algebra permissions dominate portfolio preferences.
derivative_permissions.rule: A capability mismatch is a typed unsupported route, never a hidden fallback.

fallback.commit_boundary: Fallback is transactional at a committed time boundary. No partially converged candidate state is exposed.
fallback.complete_work: Charge all failed speculation, rejected steps, setup, startup, preconditioner and fallback work.
fallback.permission: Fallback must obey the same user derivative/linear algebra permission contract.
fallback.no_escape: No allowed fallback means typed failure with original state intact.

work_ledger.reuse_existing: Extend WorkCounters and fair-ab output authority; do not create competing definitions.
work_ledger.depth: Report method-stage DAG depth, inner solver iteration/reduction depth and scheduling/communication separately.

spatial_contract.MOL: Support M(t) ydot=F(t,y) only for methods that declare mass-matrix capability.
spatial_contract.separation: Spatial discretization owns geometry, mesh/topology, basis, boundary conditions, mass matrix, conservation fluxes and spatial norm. Temporal solver owns time integration and temporal history.
spatial_contract.geometry_norm: Do not assume Cartesian Euclidean WRMS on a sphere/surface. Use declared quadrature/volume weights and physical-output metrics.
spatial_contract.parallel_axes: Spatial row/element/domain decomposition is not temporal stage parallelism.
